guide.summary: Per-user OAuth fits customers from other workspaces when the integration is public. The only needed grant is read content, and access is limited to pages each customer selects in the page picker.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles and content of pages customers explicitly share with the app. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Each customer authorizes via OAuth 2.0 and the user picks pages
findings.detail: OAuth integrations use OAuth 2.0. Each user goes through the authorization flow, selects pages in the page picker, and the app receives a user-tied access token used for subsequent API requests. Each user must authorize individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers in other workspaces connect and only explicitly shared pages are read.

evidence.quote: a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

findings.title: Public integration needed for workspaces outside a fixed installation scope
findings.detail: A scoped integration can be installed only in selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Making the app available to any workspace requires a public integration. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.

findings.title: Read content capability for reading page titles and content
findings.detail: Calls to read page content, such as the markdown endpoint and page retrieval, require the read content capability on the connection. Without it, the API returns 403. Each page must still be shared with the connection through the page picker.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads titles and content of customer-shared pages; this is the least-privilege read capability for the confirmed read-only request.

evidence.quote: your connection, open the Configuration tab, and scroll to the Capabilities section. Attempting to call this endpoint without read content capabilities returns an HTTP response with a 403 status code.
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .
Once the connection is shared, you can start making API requests. If the page is not shared, any API requests made will respond with an error.

findings.title: Marketplace review is not required to start OAuth authorization
findings.detail: Authorization can start once client credentials and the redirect URI are configured. Marketplace submission or review is not required for this flow. Listing details are managed separately.
findings.appliesWhen: Only if the app is listed on the Marketplace; not required to begin authorization.

evidence.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review
Marketplace listing details (such as descriptions, categories, and images) are managed separately through the Listings section. Refer to the List on the Marketplace guide to learn more.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: In the Developer portal under Build > Connections, create a new connection with OAuth enabled, a redirect URI, and installation scope set to any workspace (public integration) because customers from other workspaces will connect. Installation scope cannot be changed later.
steps.doneWhen: The connection exists with a public installation scope, a redirect URI registered, and the OAuth client ID and client secret visible on the Configuration tab.

steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives a code query parameter after the customer selects pages and clicks Allow access.

steps.title: Read a customer-shared page as markdown
steps.detail: Call the markdown endpoint with the customer's access token for a page the customer selected. The response's markdown field is the page content. If truncated is true, the unknown_block_ids field lists blocks to fetch separately.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 with object page_markdown and a non-empty markdown string for a shared page. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Read a shared page's title from page properties
steps.detail: Call the page retrieve endpoint for the same shared page. The title is the property whose type is title inside the properties object of the page response. Use the property key returned for that title property (commonly named title or Name) and read its title array, joining all text segments.
steps.doneWhen: The response is 200 with object page and the title property's title array yields the page title text. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

blockers.title: Read titles and content of pages customers explicitly share with the app
blockers.resolution: Setup, the read content capability, both concrete GET requests and the unshared-page 404 boundary check are documented, but read-page-markdown must re-call GET /v1/pages/{unknown_block_id}/markdown for each unknown_block_ids entry when truncated is true and append the results (inaccessible IDs return 404), and read-page-title must take the title from the properties entry whose type is title, joining its title[].plain_text segments, and follow the page property item endpoint with next_cursor while has_more is true for titles exceeding 25 mentions. Affected steps: read-page-markdown, read-page-title.
